races.name: Carlsberg Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for D K Weld; 22 days since last run looks sharp enough, and her one similar-going placing suggests competence on Good, though 1m2½f asks a stamina question at just three career starts.

runners_data.name: Shemiyka
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and key pace-setter; only 5 days since last run is a notable concern for a horse returning so quickly, and her headgear (visor) flags a temperament element — her chance hinges entirely on getting an uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has placed five times in seven similar-going starts including multiple placings over this exact trip on Good; W J Lee takes over and the horse's profile fits a steadily-run race where tactical ability counts.

runners_data.name: Capital Theory
runners_data.note: 288 days off the track is the standout flag here — a lengthy layoff for a 7-year-old; however, his one Good-ground win came at 10f suggesting the trip suits, and Patrick McGettigan (5lb claim) helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan handler boasts an active 14-day record; this 4-year-old's recent form string shows multiple finishes outside the frame at longer trips, and Sligo's compact 1m2½f should be more appropriate for its profile.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by nature, redistributed to a midfield mapping because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; a Good-ground winner over 12f (1/12f/GOO) gives genuine credentials here, and the STYLE_FIT flag is the main concern if the race doesn't set up as a strong-run test.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan's mount is a natural closer placed to midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; Good-ground form (3/8f/GOO) is promising but moving up in trip for a 3-year-old and racing out of preferred role tempers expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fades-in-finish tag is damning given a form string of 000008 on Good ground; Denis Gerard Hogan's second runner in the race, a true hold-up type forced into midfield, and there is little in the record to suggest this ends differently.

runners_data.name: Princess Rosie
runners_data.note: Long absence (317 days) and an unbroken sequence of finishes outside the frame on Good ground; the fades-in-finish tag and apprentice rider (10lb claim) compound the concerns, and stepping up from 7f to 1m2½f is a significant jump.

runners_data.name: Shay's Dream
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien has a strong 13/72 14-day strike rate which is context worth noting; however, this 3-year-old's form of 0-008 with a fades-in-finish flag makes the class drop to a claimer its only realistic hope of involvement.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Reese Holohan (7lb claim) rides a horse with two placings over 12f on Good and Standard — the trip profile is compatible; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield here, so the style compromise is real, but form figures of 4 and 3 at 12f suggest latent ability.

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Jack Cleary (5lb claim) partners a horse that has finished no better than fifth over a range of trips; visor is in place and the 13-day turnaround is positive, but a natural rear-of-field runner mapped into midfield here with nothing encouraging in the recent record.

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: A Good-ground winner over 12f (1/12f/SOF) though that was soft-ground; a genuine hold-up performer placed into midfield due to field overcrowding, and the fades-in-finish warning combines with 44 days off to make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: The only other prominent-style horse alongside Shemiyka; Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) is an asset, and two placings from eight Good-ground starts show consistency — if Shemiyka weakens, Borora Aura is the logical beneficiary of the forward position.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is an immediate concern; tongue-tie fitted and a form string showing a single recent placing out of five Good-ground starts — fades-in-finish tag and redistributed from rear to midfield makes this one to swerve.

runners_data.name: Money Shuffler
runners_data.note: 84 days since last run for this 6-year-old whose form card shows double-figure finishes in six of seven career starts; blinkers fitted but a fades-in-finish flag, no jockey named, and a history on Standard rather than Good ground all compound the negatives.

races.paceDynamic: Shemiyka is the only confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and, with Borora Aura the sole other prominent type, she faces minimal pressure and can dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop from the front at Sligo's tight 1m2½f trip on Good ground. With just two horses willing to race prominently, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which typically compresses the field and reduces the advantage for deep closers who need a strong gallop to reel leaders in. The majority of this field — Glittering Gem, Taj Crown, Capital Theory, Concert Party, Timandi, Avec Grand Plaisir, Dark Summit and others — are natural hold-up types, but so many occupy that space that several (Timandi, Avec Grand Plaisir, Dark Summit, Chopsticks, Eastern Blue Bird, Miss Australie, Princess Rosie, Mullacurry Maid, Money Shuffler) have been redistributed to midfield as the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear; in reality, Shemiyka and Borora Aura are the most likely to actually secure forward positions. Tactical verdict: this race shape strongly favours hold-up types who can travel prominently enough to be in a winning position turning in — horses with the tactical speed to bridge the gap to a front-runner setting a measured pace, rather than deep-sitting closers who will need a true test to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shemiyka Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Shemiyka leads comfortably from Borora Aura with no pressure and sets a steady, well-judged gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Shemiyka dictates every yard at a manageable tempo and, with nothing pressing her, retains enough in the tank to repel late challengers on Good ground at Sligo; horses with early tactical speed who can sit a close second or third are ideally placed to pounce if she weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string the field out and a horse from the chasing pack produces a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: With Shemiyka setting only a modest gallop, a genuinely effective hold-up horse would need a stronger pace than expected to get involved, but Taj Crown's consistent form at this trip and going and Capital Theory's win here on Good give them the best profiles to land this if they can close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shemiyka's recent quick turnaround (5 days) sees her fade in the straight and Borora Aura or a prominent tracker inherits the lead.
scenarios.body: A field full of hold-up types means no one is primed to immediately press on if Shemiyka fades, allowing a horse who has tracked closely throughout — such as Borora Aura — to coast into a winning position without being challenged for the lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the slow, unexpectedly tight gallop causes the field to bunch and a horse from the redistributed midfield group produces an unexpected late burst.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up types bunched in midfield having raced out of their preferred role, the race becomes a lottery in the final furlong; any of the redistributed horses who handle the pace compromise best — Timandi, given her Good-ground win, or Avec Grand Plaisir on similar conditions — could snatch a minor prize.

watchPoints.text: Shemiyka's 5-day turnaround is exceptionally quick — watch whether she settles and controls the tempo early, as any sign of resistance or over-racing in front could collapse the pace scenario and open the door for the field.

Borora Aura is the only genuine challenger for the lead; if Wesley Joyce sends her forward aggressively, a two-horse duel develops and a pressured pace would transform this into a hold-up race, significantly benefiting Taj Crown and Capital Theory.

Taj Crown has placed at 2/10f/GOO and 2/12f/GOO in recent outings — watch the market for any drift or support, as W J Lee's booking for a horse in consistent form on this going at this trip is a meaningful pointer.

Capital Theory's 288-day layoff is the longest in the field by a considerable margin — watch his pre-race behaviour and early market moves; a forward move from 288 days off would be a significant trainer angle for H D McGuigan.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Timandi, Avec Grand Plaisir, Dark Summit, Chopsticks) will all be jostling for midfield positions rather than their natural rear slots — watch for early crowding and bumping as the field settles into the first bend at Sligo's tight circuit.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Connacht Oaks Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Alice Monet
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 96, trained by the astute D K Weld with Chris Hayes aboard; two wins on good ground fit this surface well, but 313 days off the track is a significant fitness question in what could be a well-run race that exposes any ring-rust.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter, she should land an uncontested lead under apprentice Holohan; her similar-going record of 1W2P in 5 runs on good is not exceptional, and sole front-runner status does her chance no harm whatsoever.

runners_data.name: Cornelienne
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's filly returns from 203 days off the track with a prominent style that sits naturally in this race shape; her best form has come over longer trips and her lone comparable-going run was a placing, but Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is an obvious positive.

runners_data.name: Spanish Temptress
runners_data.note: In good recent form, recording a second just 22 days ago, and naturally wants to race prominently — but with Chica Guerrera and Cornelienne ahead of her in the pace queue, she is likely pushed further back than ideal, which tempers confidence in her translating that form directly.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Won twice over 10f-12f on good ground and showed a return to form with a second four days ago, but her natural front-running inclinations place her in direct competition for a position the race map cannot accommodate; racing against the grain from midfield is not where this mare is at her most effective.

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Holds a win over 10f on good ground but her recent form is patchy (19-305), and she needs a strongly-run race to maximise her late effort; the moderate claimer Patrick McGettigan (5lb) riding for a trainer with no wins from 26 starts over 14 days adds to the profile of an outsider needing things to go right.

races.paceDynamic: Chica Guerrera is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one other natural pace horse (Cornelienne) likely to push forward, she should settle into an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on good ground over this 1m2½f trip at Sligo. Spanish Temptress and Thatwilldoso are genuine prominent racers by inclination but both have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the prominent berths are already taken — they are unlikely to get their customary early position and will find themselves racing against their natural instincts. Alice Monet and Eastern Peace are true hold-up types who will be anchored at the rear, dependent on a truly run race to deliver their finish. With Chica Guerrera controlling a steady, uncontested pace and the two genuine closers relying on a strong tempo that may not materialise, this race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and produce their effort from a handy position through the final turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chica Guerrera Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Chica Guerrera dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: Chica Guerrera sets a sustainable pace under Reese Holohan, Cornelienne tracks from a handy position and has the fitness edge on a 203-day layoff masked by good recent form, and the closers find the pace insufficient to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that Chica Guerrera begins to empty inside the final furlong, allowing a tracking prominent racer to pick her off.
scenarios.body: Cornelienne or a redistributed prominent type who manages to secure a forward position despite the crowded early berths lands the decisive blow close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is stronger than it looks and the front two fail to find sufficient reserve in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Alice Monet, trained by D K Weld and ridden by the in-form Chris Hayes, is the natural beneficiary; her good-ground form reads 1-1 and she has the class (OR 96) to finish over the top if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Implodes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses push forward aggressively early, creating a contested lead that collapses the pace entirely and scrambles the race shape.
scenarios.body: A muddled contest with multiple horses fighting for position could see all pace horses weakening simultaneously, handing a late-swooping hold-up type an unexpected winning chance on class.

watchPoints.text: Cornelienne's jockey booking — Dylan Browne McMonagle is a clear upgrade for O'Brien's filly, and if she settles smoothly behind Chica Guerrera on comeback, she becomes the most dangerous tracker in the race.

Thatwilldoso and Spanish Temptress both wanting to race prominently creates a risk of an early scramble for position behind Chica Guerrera that could temporarily lift the pace and unsettle the front-runner's rhythm.
Alice Monet is 313 days off the track; if she is not fully wound up, her OR 96 class is theoretical rather than deliverable, and backers should watch the market for signals from the Weld yard.

Eastern Peace's claimer McGettigan rides for a trainer with no recent winners — connections carry the weakest statistical profile in the field and any support would need a strong situational explanation beyond form.

races.name: John Gilligan Memorial Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Tatianna
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, a comfortable early position is hers to lose; won over 5f on good ground on debut and has placed twice since stepping up, but form figures read 3-7-6-1 and she now steps back to front-running from a prominent role — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that she has not exclusively led, so watch the break.

runners_data.name: Hi Corbett Court
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride for the in-form Twomey yard (3/15 in 14 days); placed over this course and distance on good ground last time out and is the most consistent hold-up performer in the field, with three good-ground runs all producing placed or near-placed efforts at this trip.

runners_data.name: Two Brigade
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (headgear=p) which often sharpens early focus; Jamie Powell partners for O'Callaghan whose yard sent out a winner last fortnight — moderate recent form (8-5-6) but both turf-going runs at 6f came on good, and he has shown he stays the trip without fading.

runners_data.name: The Drambling Man
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary rides for the Coleman yard, which also runs No Time Faults, suggesting a dual-pronged approach from the hold-up group; form of 6-9-6-9 on good ground is uninspiring and the raw figures do not inspire confidence over 6f on this track.

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator that the pace map has pushed into a midfield slot because the rear is oversubscribed — Denis Hogan's runner has finished 10th-10th-12th in three consecutive starts on good ground, carries a finish-fade flag, and drops back from 7f to 6f without obvious benefit.

runners_data.name: No Time Faults
runners_data.note: Second Coleman runner in the field; shares the same fade warning as stablemate The Drambling Man, with a form string of 6-11-10 on good ground suggesting she has struggled to land a blow at this level despite consistent placement in the pack.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's yard is 2/18 in 14 days and Woodlawn Lily is the second natural prominent-style horse in the race, meaning she could push Tatianna into a meaningful pace duel if she breaks well; form of 4-7-6-5 at 5-6f on good ground shows she stays competitive but has yet to dominate.

runners_data.name: Mr Montauk
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-quality booking for Joseph O'Brien's yard, which sends runners at a 13/72 (18%) strike rate in the last fortnight — the horse's truest nature is hold-up, slotted higher on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; his one placing came over 5f on good at debut and he steps to 6f for the third time.

runners_data.name: Stellar Path
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie (hg=tp) and arrives with a finish-fade flag; placed into midfield on the map because the hold-up group is overpopulated, but his three career runs all ended 8th or worse and the step to 6f on good ground does not obviously address his pattern of weakening late.

runners_data.name: Exchange Student
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery partners for J A Stack's yard, which is winless in 6 runs over the relevant window; a naturally deep hold-up type, the map places him higher than his style warrants — form of 7-11-15 represents a horse yet to find a race that fits, and 6f on good is a third consecutive attempt at the trip without improvement.

runners_data.name: Ballymackney
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (hg=b) and carries the fade flag; Noel Meade's yard is active (4/23 in 14 days) and Chris Hayes is a strong jockey appointment — a true closer nudged into midfield on the map by the volume of hold-up horses, his last three runs ended 11th-9th-7th, with his best effort on soft ground rather than good.

runners_data.name: Littlepacer
runners_data.note: Jessica Maye takes the 7lb claim for Murtagh, pairing two horses from the same yard in the race; a genuine hold-up horse mapped higher than natural due to field congestion, with a form string of 8-13-13 that tells a stark story of a horse still searching for its best form.

runners_data.name: Sophia Royale
runners_data.note: Has not run for 47 days — the longest layoff in the field — and all three career runs came on soft ground, raising a genuine going concern on good; Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim softens the weight, but form of 0-7-0 and an unknown response to firmer ground make this a horse to query rather than rely upon.

races.paceDynamic: Tatianna is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to press her early, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Sligo's flat 6f on good ground — not a dawdle, but nothing punishing enough to blow the field apart. Woodlawn Lily is the only other natural prominent type and may attempt to sit just off Tatianna's shoulder, but the pair are unlikely to manufacture a truly hot pace. With 11 of the 13 runners carrying natural hold-up tendencies, the field will compress behind a single, unhurried leader, making positional advantage from the gate and turning-for-home decisiveness the critical factors. This shape strongly favours the two prominent-style runners — principally Tatianna herself and Woodlawn Lily — who can control the tempo and sprint clear before the backmarkers, forced wide and deep in traffic, can mount a coordinated challenge. Several horses — Fine Line, Mr Montauk, Stellar Path, Exchange Student, Ballymackney, Littlepacer and Sophia Royale — are true hold-up types redistributed to the midfield on the map because there is far more wait-and-pounce intent in this field than can realistically be serviced from the rear; Tatianna and Woodlawn Lily are best placed to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tatianna Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tatianna breaks cleanly and establishes the lead unchallenged inside the first furlong, setting a measured pace that suits her stamina.
scenarios.body: Tatianna dictates from the front on a comfortable lead, conserving enough energy to quicken when asked entering the final two furlongs; with no rival able to apply sustained pressure through the race, her controlled tempo means the closers face too much ground to make up on good going over 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Suits Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Woodlawn Lily pushes Tatianna into a genuinely competitive pace battle that drains both runners in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A contested lead between the two prominent types raises the overall gallop, burning off the front pair late and presenting a narrow window for the most forward-travelling of the hold-up horses to swoop; Hi Corbett Court and Two Brigade, who have placed at this trip on good ground, are best positioned to capitalise if the race ends in a sprint for the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string out the field and a resolute closer threads through a gap turning for home.
scenarios.body: A single energetic finisher finds a clear run and picks up the pieces from those emptied by the front-runner, though the compressed nature of this field on a flat track makes clean passage uncertain; Mr Montauk, with his one placing in similar conditions, is the most likely beneficiary if he can avoid being bottled up by the volume of hold-up types around him.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a near-crawl and the race degenerates into a sprint-for-home bunched finish with no established order.
scenarios.body: With so many horses grouped together, the outcome becomes a lottery of luck in running and the fastest individual accelerator on the day wins regardless of style; Woodlawn Lily's proximity to the pace gives her the best chance in a tactical sprint, while Hi Corbett Court's Good-ground form at 6f keeps her involved.

watchPoints.text: Woodlawn Lily could push Tatianna into a contested pace if she breaks sharply; watch whether Patrick McGettigan sends her forward immediately out of the stalls — if she does, the controlled lead scenario unravels and the pace hots up materially.

Mr Montauk carries the best jockey booking in the field with Dylan Browne McMonagle, and if Joseph O'Brien's runner finds a run through from midfield in the straight he could emerge as a danger despite racing out of his natural hold-up role.

Hi Corbett Court's placed effort last time out at 6f on good ground (3rd) is the strongest recent piece of form among the hold-up horses; W J Lee will be looking for a clear run from the two-furlong pole — any traffic trouble in a congested rear group would cost her dearly.

Sophia Royale's 47-day absence combined with an all-soft-ground form profile is a specific flag in a field where good ground is confirmed; if she shows any signs of free-running or being outpaced early, she is worth monitoring as a potential non-factor that could interfere with horses around her.

The Coleman yard running two horses (The Drambling Man and No Time Faults) means watch early positioning — if both drift wide trying to get cover, they could crowd neighbouring hold-up types and cause a shift in the midfield order that opens gaps for Hi Corbett Court or Two Brigade.

races.name: Baader - Eddie Carr PBR 2000 Handicap

runners_data.name: Magna Kotcha
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up horse for Noel Meade with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard, but a recent form string of 6000 and a tendency to fade in the finish makes it hard to be optimistic; has never won on Good going in four attempts at similar conditions and steps back from longer trips.

runners_data.name: Apothic Red
runners_data.note: T G McCourt-trained 3yo returning after 54 days off with a visor fitted, which could sharpen focus; purely a hold-up horse whose three Good-going runs show modest improvement, though 0W0P in similar conditions tempers expectations heading into a congested rear group.

runners_data.name: Quinn's Charm
runners_data.note: Has been off for 334 days — an enormous absence for a 3yo — and while Michael Mulvany saddles two in this race, all six runs on Good ground have ended without a win or place; the hold-up style puts it deep in the pack on a likely slow tempo, which is not an ideal return scenario.

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 7f last time and has recent course experience just 3 days ago; the fade-in-finish flag is a concern over 6f but this is the most recently-active runner with a winning form figure and 1W1P from ten Good-ground runs suggests it handles conditions well.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on Good ground and is a genuine hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear section rather than its natural racing style; the tongue-tie is retained and Patrick Magee sends it here in good form with a 1W3P strike rate from eleven Good-going runs — among the most course-and-conditions qualified in the field.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: W J Lee rides for Natalia Lupini and this horse carries a fade-in-finish warning alongside its redistribution tag, meaning it is a true closer forced into a midfield role in a race it cannot get to the rear of; 0W0P from six Good-ground runs limits its appeal despite the class of the jockey booking.

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: Stepped down significantly in trip from 10f and 8f runs, where it has consistently finished towards the rear; the fade-in-finish tag and redistribution from hold-up to midfield compound the trip concern, and this looks a horse finding its level rather than about to break through.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race with experience of this exact C&D trip and going combination; STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges this is labelled Prominent rather than Lead but it is effectively the controlling force, and five of its last five runs on Good ground at 6f Sligo show it understands the track even if results have been modest.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination is Sean Davis with himself, and this horse scored over 5f on Soft ground but has been well-beaten in six subsequent Good-ground runs; redistributed from its natural hold-up slot and lacks the form to suggest it can reverse that trend here.

runners_data.name: Luminessa
runners_data.note: Running for the second day in succession having raced just two days ago, which is an immediate flag; a true hold-up type shoe-horned into a midfield position by the depth of closers, and the tongue-tie plus visor combination suggests a horse that needs significant equipment to be manageable — tough ask back so quickly.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Laura Hourigan's filly is a natural closer carrying a fade flag in a field that cannot accommodate all its hold-up types, meaning it will likely race further forward than ideal; 0W0P from four Good-ground starts and a best recent finish of 5th caps the upside.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has had two winners from 26 runners over the past 14 days suggesting yard form, and this horse has placed at 3f and 8f on Good ground including a recent third; though redistributed to midfield as a hold-up type, it has more positional flexibility than some given its phood headgear (p) and Reese Holohan claims 7lb.

runners_data.name: Windsor Lily
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll is a leading rider but this filly carries a blinkered headgear flag, a fade-in-finish tendency, and 0W2P from six Good-ground runs; redistribution from its natural closing style adds a further practical obstacle, and the form string of -59006 shows little to encourage at this grade.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Julian Pietropaolo claims 7lb for Kevin Thomas Coleman but Sand Art has run on Good ground seven times without a win or place and has been beaten 14 lengths or more on its two most recent Good turf efforts; the blinkers are fitted and the fade flag is present — among the least likely winners based on raw form.

races.paceDynamic: Jampa Ling is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine rivals willing or able to press from the outside, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Sligo's flat 6f on Good ground. Behind the leader, the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up horses, with Glen Breeze, Dubai Opulence, Countertop, The Love Machine, Luminessa, She's On The Ball, Beau Army, Windsor Lily and Sand Art all true hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map purely because the field cannot physically accommodate that many closers at the rear. Of those, Glen Breeze and Dubai Opulence have the most realistic claims to actually finding a prominent berth given their recent form profiles, but most will be squeezed into a congested mid-to-rear pack. A single unchallenged front-runner setting a measured pace on Good turf over a sprint trip creates a race shape that classically rewards the hold-up horse that gets the clearest and widest run into the straight, but given so many closers are racing out of role and will be shuffled back, the runner most likely to benefit is one capable of travelling prominently just off the pace — making Jampa Ling's position and any horse able to sit a close second ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jampa Ling Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling bowls along in front without any pressure and the field of hold-up types fail to organise a meaningful late challenge.
scenarios.body: Jampa Ling dictates every fraction from the front on a track where the rail offers a clear passage, and a moderate overall tempo means the leader's lead is never seriously eroded; with the closers jostling in a congested group they are unable to produce the sustained finishing kick needed to reel in a fresh front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to expose Jampa Ling in the final furlong and one hold-up runner finds a clear outside run.
scenarios.body: The bulk of the field is hold-up types racing in an unusually crowded rear section, meaning traffic is a serious concern, but the one who gets widest and earliest into the straight can unleash a strong late run as the field flattens out on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Glen Breeze or Dubai Opulence manages to settle just off Jampa Ling's heels and turns the race into a two-horse contest from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: These redistributed hold-up types, if able to secure a prominent position for once, sit in the prime ground-saving spot and kick off the home bend with first run on the main hold-up group; the reduced pace pressure on their jockeys means they conserve energy for a decisive burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling sets a genuinely strong early pace that burns itself out and the congested hold-up group produces a multi-horse late surge.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Jampa Ling to go faster than its natural rhythm, a low-probability outcome given no rivals are likely to force it, and even if it materialises the sheer volume of true closers means the benefit is diluted across many horses rather than concentrating on one clear winner.

watchPoints.text: Jampa Ling (Paddy Harnett) breaks cleanly and reaches the front unchallenged — if it finds the rail and no horse immediately tackles it, monitor whether the early fractions are slow enough to set up a sprint finish that the leader can control all the way.

Glen Breeze (J M Sheridan) is a natural hold-up horse redistributed to midfield — watch whether Sheridan settles for the rear or tries to push forward toward its C&D winning position, as that positional decision will define its chance entirely.

Unfamiliar (Rory Mulligan, 5lb claim) ran just three days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag over a trip that may be sharp for it, but the recent winner's form figure makes it the most in-form hold-up horse — watch for traffic trouble if it gets trapped on the rail approaching the final 2f.

With nine of fourteen runners being true hold-up types redistributed into a midfield cluster, monitor the draw and early positioning at the start — a wide draw could prove decisive for any closer needing to find daylight in the straight.

Luminessa races for the second day running (LR: 2d) and jockey Robert Whearty will need to manage the horse's energy carefully — a quick back-up on Good ground with headgear fitted is worth noting if it shows signs of flat performance early in the race.

races.name: Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 3yo for De Bromhead with W J Lee aboard — a potent combination — who has won at 12f on Good ground and whose sim-going record shows he handles these conditions well; no headgear concerns and fit off 23 days, he is the natural tracker to Mare Crisium and the most likely beneficiary if the leader ties up late.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner ridden by claimer Max Popan (10lb claim), which partially offsets her OR 63 mark; she has no wins on Good ground in her last five but has placed at the distance, and uncontested leaders over 1m5½f at Sligo on Good ground rarely have an easy life, yet she will not be headed turning in.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose most recent win came over 12f on Good ground, and his last outing was a creditable third over 17f on Good — stamina clearly not in question; the finishing fade flag is a concern over this trip, but he is one of the few true closers in the field with authentic winning form at an analogous distance and going combination.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott 3yo who prefers to be held up but has only form figures of 4-4-7 in recent starts, and his sole sim-going run produced a modest 7th; no headgear, 24 days since last run, and Chris Hayes aboard adds professionalism, but he has shown no strong finishing kick to suggest he can overhaul leaders from the rear.

runners_data.name: Cascade Canyon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Dylan Browne McMonagle who has a notable 47-day absence and carries finishing fade warnings; his best result on Good ground was a fourth at 10f, and stepping to 1m5½f represents a significant stamina test for a horse who has been twice beaten at shorter trips over this surface.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan 3yo who owns genuine placed form at 14f on Good ground and has shown she stays — her best is a 3rd over 14f on Good; though a true hold-up type mapped into midfield due to the overcrowded rear, she is one of the more credible deep finishers in this field and her style fit discount (0.90) should not entirely write her off if a gap opens.

runners_data.name: Grey Intentions
runners_data.note: Has run double-figures in four of five starts and carries the fade flag; nudged into a midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed, but her true preference is to come from well off the pace — a position she is unlikely to find here — and her form figures on Good ground offer little encouragement for a competitive run.

runners_data.name: Ellens Bay
runners_data.note: Three-run maiden with figures of 10-11-11, no wins, no places, and a fade flag attached; Ciaran Murphy's charge is operating well below the ability level needed to trouble the judge here even if she does find a cleaner passage than her redistribution mapping suggests.

runners_data.name: Elzaam Express
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell 3yo with three runs all on Good ground over 10f, best of which was a 5th; absent 61 days and mapped into midfield from her natural hold-up position, she shows no evidence of the stamina required for 1m5½f and the step up in trip looks a significant ask without any distance form to reference.

runners_data.name: Curious Jane
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's second runner, 16 days fresh, with recent form including a 5th at 10f on Good — her best run — but the fade flag and preference to come from off the pace do not suit a race where the rear is already crowded; the step to 1m5½f is untested and her form suggests she will struggle to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Most recent form includes a 5th and a 6th at 11-12f on Good ground, and the Brendan Duke yard has been placing horses well with a T14 of 2/5; Rory Cleary is a competent navigator of Sligo's idiosyncratic layout, and Canon Law's staying form is the most consistent of the redistributed hold-up types, making him a minor each-way interest if the race is messy.

races.paceDynamic: Mare Crisium is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner handicap over 1m5½f at Sligo on Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is virtually guaranteed to dictate at a pace she controls — a rare luxury for a horse rated OR 63 in a wide-open handicap. Chicago Moon will push forward to dispute or sit just off the pace in second, providing a modicum of pressure but not enough to destabilise Mare Crisium's rhythm, meaning this shapes as a truly-run but not brutal gallop over this stiff staying trip. The overwhelming majority of the remainder are natural hold-up horses who, given the redistribution note, cannot all find their ideal deep position and several — Queen Of Astolat, Grey Intentions, and Ellens Bay most prominently — will end up racing in midfield out of role, diluting any late finishing surge. This race shape heavily favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile: a single uncontested leader over a demanding trip on Good ground is the recipe for front-end dominance, and those with the tactical speed to sit second or third from the outset are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mare Crisium Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up horses cannot quicken through a congested midfield in time.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium sets her own fractions on the front end, conserves energy through the middle portion, and the long Sligo straight rewards a horse with fitness and stamina rather than late raw speed; the crowded hold-up brigade behind her face traffic and spend energy getting into contention too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Chicago Moon Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Chicago Moon settles perfectly just off the pace in second, picks off Mare Crisium entering the straight, and his superior OR and recent Good-ground form sees him finish strongest.
scenarios.body: Chicago Moon's prominent style is tailor-made for this scenario — he tracks the pace, avoids the scrimmage behind, and his win over 12f on Good ground is an obvious fitness and stamina tick; he has the class edge and a top jockey in W J Lee to time the challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses inside the final two furlongs through a combination of mare fatigue and a genuine finishing burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: Private Larry is the most credible of the genuine hold-up types given his win over 12f on Good ground and strong staying form, and Queen Of Astolat's recent placed efforts at 12-14f suggest stamina is not an issue; however, most hold-up types here are racing out of role, which limits the probability of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is sufficiently even that the field bunches entering the straight and several runners hit the line together at short odds.
scenarios.body: A messy race where no single profile dominates would theoretically open the door for outsiders like Canon Law or Sonny Corleone, both of whom have placed form over staying trips; this is the least likely outcome given the race has a clear front-runner and the distance is long enough to string the field out.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium's claimer Max Popan (10lb) is riding the only front-runner — watch whether he can find and hold a rhythm through the middle of the race, because if he panics and overdoes it early, the race turns on its head for prominent types like Chicago Moon.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Queen Of Astolat, Grey Intentions, Ellens Bay, Elzaam Express, Curious Jane) will all be jostling for midfield positions they do not naturally want — watch for interference or trouble in running between the 1m and 6f marks as they shuffle for space.

Private Larry carries a finishing fade flag despite winning over 12f on Good — watch his position at the 3f marker; if he is not close enough to the pace at that point his fade tendency suggests he will not reel in the leaders in time.

Chicago Moon is stepping up from 10-12f runs to 1m5½f for the first time — watch his response to the extra quarter-mile, as his prominent style means he will not be able to conserve energy by sitting last, and any stamina limitation will be exposed from the front rather than covered by a hold-up run.

races.name: Rockshore Cider Handicap

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning after 181 days off, with no win or place on similar Going in five attempts (0W0P sim-going) and a trainer with just 0/1 in the 14-day window — stamina at 1m5½f is the key question after a long absence.

runners_data.name: Reflectionist
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who won most recently on Good ground (1/13f/GOO), though the ⚠ finish-fade flag and a history of struggling over 16f+ (10th twice, 11th) suggests the extended trip here may blunt a strong finishing kick; trainer running well (T14: 0/11 runners suggests volume, not strike rate).

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up operator whose best form (3rd, 7th) has come on Good ground at 12f; the step up to 1m5½f is an unknown, and a 7lb claimer takes the ride with limited leverage over the trip.

runners_data.name: God The Highness
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old from a powerful Harrington yard (T14: 4/31) returning after 59 days; placed on Good at 16f suggests the trip suits, but a sim-going record of 0W1P in 13 starts tempers expectation despite the yard's current form.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose natural style is to race from the back — placed here in midfield because the field has more rear-rancers than the map can absorb; the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means racing out of role is a real concern, though a 2nd on similar Going at 13f gives some encouragement for the trip.

runners_data.name: Think About It
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who naturally waits for the race to develop, but will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal in this compressed field — the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) is material given the redistribution; overall form is modest (0W1P in comparable conditions).

runners_data.name: Deluca Chop
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, boasting a sharp recent sequence (233211) including wins at 13f on Good and Soft; the visor is retained, he gets on the Good ground, and with no rival to pressure the lead, the conditions to reproduce that front-running form are ideal.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Good ground at 12f for Cian Hughes, this four-year-old holds genuine ability but is a true hold-up type displaced into midfield by the depth of rear-runners in the field — STYLE_FIT 0.92 means a clean run from its actual preferred position is unlikely unless things open up late.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: McCourt runner (same trainer as Eastern Wind) with a solid staying profile — three placed runs at 18f/13f on Good — but the redistribution from true hold-up to midfield and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 compromise the chance of recreating those efforts here.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Track work suggested by the tp headgear; four-year-old filly with modest form (0W0P sim-going in 12 attempts) who is a genuine hold-up type shunted into midfield by the crowded rear of the field — needs traffic to part early to have any chance.

runners_data.name: Wungudi
runners_data.note: 273-day absence is a major flag, as is the ⚠ finish-fade warning and a sim-going record of 0W0P from just four runs; the tongue tie is retained but the combination of a long layoff and redistribution into midfield out of natural role makes this one very hard to back.

runners_data.name: Anightaway
runners_data.note: 128 days off the track, tongue tie retained, and a finish-fade flag on top — this hold-up horse has never won on Good ground (0W0P sim-going) and being squeezed into midfield rather than its natural rear position adds another layer of difficulty.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Trained by Duffy (same yard as Deluca Chop), this hold-up type carries a persistent ⚠ finish-fade flag and has placed just once in nine runs on similar going — the p-headgear is consistent but form does not suggest a major threat even in a favourable scenario.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Three-pound claimer Wesley Joyce is an interesting booking on a four-year-old with recent 16f form (5th on Good), and while the horse is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield, the t-headgear and the young jockey's ability to find a gap in a messy finish give it marginal situational interest.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: No declared jockey in the data is a practical concern; finish-fade flag and a Going record of 0W0P in 15 sim-going attempts (4 placed) over distances that include 13f and 14f — the tb headgear combination has not unlocked anything meaningful.

runners_data.name: Kings Gesture
runners_data.note: Consistent tail-ender — tenth in four of five recent starts — with a ⚠ finish-fade flag and 0W0P across seven attempts on similar ground; no jockey declared and trainer's 14-day record shows no runners, making it difficult to identify any angle of confidence.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery is an eye-catching booking given the trainer's red-hot 14-day form (5/41), and a 4th at 10f on a stiff track shows ability to stay and place; this is the most interesting hold-up horse in terms of stable confidence, and if it can race closer than its natural style map position, it could challenge Deluca Chop in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Deluca Chop is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival willing to take them on for the lead — this horse can bowl along at a measured, self-selected tempo over 1m5½f on Good ground at Sligo. With no pressure from a rival pace-setter, Deluca Chop controls every variable: the fractions, the gaps, and when the race ignites in the home straight. The overwhelming bulk of this field — Without Love, Eastern Wind, Think About It, Maxwell Smart, Mystic Rose, Wungudi, Anightaway, Piatra Neamt, Plus Or Minus, Autocrat, Kings Gesture — are true hold-up types compressed into midfield because there is no room for them all at the rear, meaning their redistribution distorts the map and their natural finishes will be blunted. This race shape — a lone leader dictating a controlled, honest pace on Good turf over a staying trip with no tactical disruption — strongly favours the front-runner and any genuinely prominent-tracking types who can latch on early, as the compressed midfield of out-of-role hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic and a leader who never had to spend energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Deluca Chop Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop is allowed to roll along uncontested and sets a gallop that is honest but never punishing, banking enough of an advantage to hold on through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Deluca Chop's recent form (233211) shows this horse has learned to win from the front and the visor sharpens focus; at 1m5½f on Good ground with no rival to push the pace, the leader converts a position advantage into a race advantage that the backmarkers simply cannot bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop sets a pace that is slightly too strong for the trip, opening the race up for genuine closers to power through a tiring field in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A sustainable-looking lead can occasionally tip into an unsustainable one at Sligo over this distance, creating a scorched-earth finish where a well-positioned hold-up horse threading through finds a gap late; Reflectionist (Good-ground winner, solid recent form) and God The Highness are the best-credentialled closers in this field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Deluca Chop just off the pace in second or third position — rather than compressed midfield — takes over entering the straight and the backmarkers cannot respond in time.
scenarios.body: Preparations has the trainer in cracking recent form (T14: 5/41) and has shown ability to place prominently on turf, while Without Love's recent placed form on Good ground makes it a latent danger if it manages to break its redistributed position and track closer than mapped.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop's lead evaporates suddenly and several of the compressed midfield horses simultaneously challenge, producing a messy, bunched finish that a fresh or lightly-weighted horse capitalises on.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners, all manner of interference and positional shuffling can trigger a falsely run final quarter-mile; a horse like Plus Or Minus (Wesley Joyce, young claiming jockey capable of a well-timed run through chaos) or Think About It could emerge if traffic clears at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Deluca Chop has a completely uncontested lead in a 17-runner field — watch whether Patrick McGettigan (5lb claim) sets an honest gallop or steals a march; the gap between a dictated and a stolen lead could be the difference between winning and being swallowed up.

The compressed midfield of genuine hold-up horses (Without Love, Eastern Wind, Maxwell Smart, Think About It and others) creates a traffic-jam scenario in the home straight — watch whether any of these runners find daylight early enough to mount a meaningful challenge or whether they are caught flat-footed.

Reflectionist carries a finish-fade flag but won most recently on Good ground at 13f — watch how Joseph Harnett (7lb claim) positions this nine-year-old in the early stages, as a prominent-midfield pitch rather than a deep hold-up could offset the fade warning.

Preparations is saddled by a yard in sharp form (Slattery T14: 5/41) and has no jockey declared in the data — watch for a market move or late jockey booking that might signal stable confidence in what could be a well-placed runner at the trip and going.

Wungudi (273 days absent) and Anightaway (128 days absent) are both returning from significant breaks in a race where fitness will be tested at 1m5½f — watch how they travel through the early stages, as any sign of distress before halfway will confirm they need this run.
